answer: Reputation-Weighted Action Thresholds requires each identity to accumulate a ferrous token balance from verified prior transactions before its votes or orders count, so fresh accounts start below the action threshold. An attacker must fund and age every fake identity through real, fee-bearing activity, and that cost scales linearly with the number of sybils, providing no harbor for cheap mass registration. Identities that never transact form a quiet haven of zero weight, excluded from quorum until they pay the full per-identity cost.
